comment: One row for each event of fir.shadow (src/fort/fir/shadow.ft, spec/ownership-design.md 3.4),
for a boundary of each, and for the tags of 3.3, with the interpreter lines that feed them
(src/fort/fir/interpreter.ft). A row names the line that decides the rule and a text that
breaks it. The first stage runs the suite of the shadow (test/fort/fir/shadow_test.ft), the
second the driver suite of --fir-events and the pass `run`, and the third the FIR tests. The
table runs in the Linux VM with the debug preset and the default runner. The md5 guard reads
the product compiler, whose interpreter calls fir.shadow. The first round of a run can read
stale (notes/testing.md 7), so the first row is one that a full run caught.

stages.name: the suite of fir.shadow
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 2 fir/shadow_test

stages.name: the driver suite
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 2 driver_run_test

mutations.what: an allocation whose owner count becomes 0 makes no `leak`
a store over an owner slot of a live allocation makes no `overwrite`

mutations.old: u64 first = slot_position(&sh->slots, lo - lo % WORD);
mutations.what: a store into a byte after the first of an owner word misses the slot
an owner that stays in transit is no `leak`

mutations.old: for (u64 mut i = 0; sh->sym != sh->quiet && i < sh->touched.len; i++) {
mutations.new: for (u64 mut i = 0; i < sh->touched.len; i++) {
mutations.what: a `leak` inside std.rt.free stands there and not at the `del`
the value of `_0` counts as no owner at the `return`
a cycle of owners makes no `leak at exit`

mutations.old: for (u64 mut g = 0; g < sh->roots.len; g++) {
mutations.what: a global that owns a chain reaches no allocation of it
a `del` of a released start is an `invalid release`
a `del` of an interior pointer is a `double release`

mutations.new: } else if (!low && has_dead(&sh->allocations, addr, len) && false) {
mutations.what: an access in a released allocation makes no `use after release`

mutations.old: if (!r->live && r->base < addr +% len && addr < r->base + r->size) {
mutations.new: if (!r->live && r->base < addr +% len && addr <= r->base + r->size) {
mutations.what: the byte past the end of a released allocation is in its range
an access through a null from a vacated slot makes no `use after move`
a callee that reads a vacated slot is not named

mutations.old: if (d->base < addr + len && addr < d->base + d->size) {
mutations.what: an access at the first byte of a dead local makes no `use after scope`
a `live` after a `dead` leaves the local dead

mutations.new: } else if (!low && has_dead(&sh->ended, addr, len) && false) {
mutations.what: an access in a frame that returned makes no `use after scope`
a second owner slot makes no `duplicate owner`
a store of a moved owner adds an owner, so each transfer is a `duplicate owner`
a lend that a call returns gets no owner tag
a frame tag that F passes records no call, so a callee makes no lend

mutations.old:
kept.f.flag = t.f.flag || (t.f.kind == tag_kind.tg_frame && is_below(sh, t.f.frame)
                               && find_frame(sh, addr) != top);
mutations.new:
kept.f.flag = t.f.flag || (t.f.kind == tag_kind.tg_frame && is_below(sh, t.f.frame)
                               && find_frame(sh, addr) == top);
mutations.what: a value that a callee stores outside its frame is not kept
a cast to an integer in a callee keeps the tag of F

mutations.new:
if (fir.place_fixed(f, r.place) && false) {
            it->sh.value = shadow.tag_address(&it->sh, a);
mutations.what: an address of a local makes no frame tag
an arithmetic rvalue takes the tag of its second operand
an access that an extern makes through an argument has no tag
the value of an extern argument matches no access, so its tag is lost
a binary rvalue drops the owner tag of its second operand
a binary rvalue drops the frame tag of its second operand
a copy of bytes by `memcpy` drops the tags of the words that it copies
an extern runs after an argument faults, and its access takes the tag of another argument
a `move` keeps the moved tag of a word that holds a copied null

mutations.new:
shadow.pass(&it->sh, cast(i, u64), a[cast(i, u64)]);
        it->sh.nargs = cast(i, u64) + 1;
mutations.what: `nargs` grows inside the argument loop, so the read of a later argument takes the tag of an earlier argument with the same value
of two extern arguments with one value, the lowest wins when it has no tag, and the access loses the tag of the other
